rationale.intervention_reconstruction: The hypothesis proposes thermal annealing to reduce interface coherency, whereas the paper varied the modulation period (λ) to create coherent, semicoherent, or grain-boundary-dominated interfaces. Both are different kinds of intervention.
rationale.condition_agreement: The hypothesis specifies sustained loading below ~0.4 T_m, while the paper used room-temperature nanoindentation creep at specific loading rates. Both involve mechanical creep testing, but the temperature regime and loading mode differ.
rationale.mechanism_agreement: The hypothesis invokes load partitioning and dislocation locking at coherent interfaces, whereas the paper's mechanism involves semicoherent interfaces promoting interfacial amorphization and diffusion/interface-slip creep. These are different mechanisms.
rationale.outcome_agreement: The hypothesis predicts coherent interfaces give lower creep rate, but the paper found semicoherent interfaces (M16) had the highest creep resistance. The predicted direction is opposite.
